At 11.35 a.m. 3-9-37, C.P.C.1574 accompanied by

Chih Tsau brought to the Station a male Chinese Pao Ah
You (包阿王), 40, Ningpo, s/unemployed, N.P.A. from

having placed some poisonous substance into food being
cooked by a hawker named Sung Ah Nyi (陈阿二) on the
West side of Weichow Road a few yards South of Ningpo
Road.

Enquiries made by C.D.C.172 and the undersigned
ascertained the following:-

At about 11.25 a.m. 3-9-37, the hawker Sung Ah
Nyi was attending to a customer, with his back towards
a medium sized stove, which has a large iron cooking
bowl on the top of it, inside of which some potatoes
were being boiled. As the hawker turned round he saw
the suspected person replacing the wooden cover of the
bowl and therefore immediately suspected that the
vegetables which were being cooked had been interfered
with, the suspected person was immediately seized and
detained by several bystanders who had been attracted

25/1.

to the scene due to the disturbance caused. The hawkers
then placed a quantity of the potatoes and fluid in
which they had been cooking inside an ordinary bowl and
ordered the suspect to eat same and prove that he had
not put anything of a harmful nature into the food.

The suspected person refused to eat the proffered
food, the crowd that had gathered became insistent, so
he commenced to shout and scream, resulting in a cry of
"traitor" being set up by the crowd who then commenced
to strike him about the body and face with their clen-
ched hands.

The above two mentioned Boy Scouts who were in
the vicinity then intervened and were able to gain
custody of the suspected person after explaining that
they intended taking him to Lamma Police Station,
C.P.C. 1374 subsequently attended the scene and brought
all concerned to the Station.

At the Station when the suspected person was
questioned he behaved in a very demented and erratic
manner and so was unable to supply a coherent explana-
tion of his previous actions, due to his believed con-
dition he was immediately removed to the St. Paul's
Chinese Hospital where an examination was conducted by
Dr. D.B. Cater (Canton) who issued the following cer-
tificate:- "Examination reveals no signs that would

22/3.

prove presence of nervous disease or insanity."

As a result of the above and as the quantity of
potatoes and fluid which had been offered the suspected
person to eat had been brought to this Station, permission was obtained from Mr. Mason, D.D.O. "A" Div. that

Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by [Signature]

A new organization styled the "War Time Service
Group of the Shanghai Municipality Boy Scouts' Committee"
has been established in the Wei Foong (渭風) Girls'
school, Lane 138, 22 Tatung Road. Mr. Hsu Kuo-dz
(徐國茲), Chief of the 50th Chinese Boy Scouts Corps with
headquarters in the Chinese Chamber of Commerce Building,
North Soochow Road, is in charge of the Service Group. The
Group claims to have a total of 1,600 Chinese boy scouts at
its disposal. The chief work of the Group is as follows : -
1) To maintain order in refugee camps.
2) To escort wounded soldiers and maintain order in hospitals
for wounded soldiers.
3) To propagate general precautions for public protection
during war time.
4) To take suspected traitors mobbed on streets, to the
Police or to the office of the Service Group, to be
properly dealt with.

In connection with the last mentioned item, it is
learned that between August 13 and 29, about twenty suspected
Chinese traitors were taken, instead of to the Municipal Police
or the French Police, to the office of the Service Group from
various places. On completion of investigations made
by the office of the Service Group, all were either released
or escorted to their respective homes.
